extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers and others interested in the Dame Janet Smith inquiry and BBC/Jimmy Savile investigation
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the evaluative scope and procedural criteria used in the Dame Janet Smith Review — an inquiry into Jimmy Savile's sexual misconduct and the BBC's role. Focuses on who was asked for evidence, the temporal and institutional scope, the core investigative questions, and procedural safeguards used during the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of evidence sought / witness types
rubrics_metrics.description: Called for evidence from people who were the subject of inappropriate sexual conduct by Jimmy Savile on BBC premises, or on location for the BBC; people who knew of or suspected such conduct; anyone who raised concerns about Savile's conduct within the BBC; people who worked for or with Savile on programmes at the BBC between about 1964 and 2007; people familiar with 'the culture or practices of the BBC during that time insofar as they may have been relevant to preventing or enabling the sexual abuse of children, young people or teenagers'; and people who held senior positions at the BBC who may have relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording lists specific witness categories and a temporal window (about 1964–2007). Emphasises both direct victims and those with knowledge, suspicions, or institutional insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal and institutional scope of the investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on conduct 'in connection with his work for the BBC' and people who worked with Savile on BBC programmes between about 1964 and 2007; offences that occurred at BBC premises or on BBC locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the period (~1964–2007) and ties abusive acts to BBC employment/activities and BBC premises/locations as the primary jurisdictional boundaries for the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did Savile commit acts of inappropriate sexual conduct in connection with his work for the BBC?
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary factual question asking whether Savile committed inappropriate sexual conduct linked to his BBC work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central question of factual responsibility that guides evidence collection and allegation assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Were any concerns raised within the BBC whether formally or informally about Savile’s inappropriate sexual conduct?
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative question focused on whether complaints, reports or informal concerns about Savile existed within the BBC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires review of both formal records and informal recollections or communications indicating concerns were raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: To what extent were BBC personnel aware of inappropriate sexual conduct by Savile in connection with his work for the BBC?
rubrics_metrics.description: Question probing the actual level of awareness among BBC staff regarding Savile's conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entails assessing testimony, memos, personnel actions, and contemporaneous records to measure awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: To what extent ought BBC personnel to have been aware of inappropriate sexual conduct by Savile in connection with his work for the BBC?
rubrics_metrics.description: Normative question assessing whether BBC personnel should reasonably have been aware of Savile's conduct given available information and duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compares what was known/available at the time with expected standards of duty, supervision, and reporting within the organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did the culture and practices within the BBC during the years of Savile’s employment enable Savile’s inappropriate sexual conduct to continue unchecked?
rubrics_metrics.description: Question evaluating whether institutional culture/practices permitted or failed to prevent Savile's conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires analysis of organisational norms, reporting channels, attitudes toward complaints, treatment of celebrities, and other practices that might enable abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural standard: avoid prejudicing ongoing police investigations or trials
rubrics_metrics.description: The report's publication was delayed to avoid prejudicing ongoing police investigations and a criminal trial (e.g., it was delayed so it would not prejudice the second trial of Stuart Hall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows an explicit procedural constraint: inquiry reports may need to be withheld or delayed to protect the integrity of concurrent police investigations or court proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness anonymity and reassurance to encourage testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Some interviewees gave evidence only after being assured their names would not be published as they feared reprisal; the report notes interviewees feared reprisal and an 'atmosphere of fear' existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a practice of offering anonymity/confidentiality to witnesses to secure evidence; also suggests evaluating whether fear of reprisal affected willingness to report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and quantify findings (extent, locations, victim counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review produced a detailed report (more than 700 pages) documenting that Savile had sexually abused 72 people and had raped eight people, with offences at 'virtually every one of the BBC premises at which he worked'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises thorough documentation and quantification of offences, victims, and locations as part of a comprehensive inquiry report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess staff handling of complaints and managerial response
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment that some members of BBC staff were aware of complaints against Savile but did nothing about them, citing a 'culture of not complaining' and failure to pass information to senior management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires examination of how complaints were handled, reporting pathways, memos, and whether managerial action was taken or withheld; includes evaluation of cultural barriers to reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce recommendations for reform of internal processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The report provided a number of recommendations for reform of the BBC's internal processes based on the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome-oriented criterion: an inquiry should conclude with concrete recommendations to change policies, procedures or culture to prevent recurrence; the article notes recommendations exist though it does not list them.
